# Agent Loop Principles {.unnumbered}

An agent loop joins model inference to persistent state and environmental feedback. Its architecture must make the system boundary explicit: the runtime needs to know what objective is active, which state is authoritative, which actions are available, and which observations justify continuing.

::: {#pri-trajectory-closure .callout-principle title="Trajectory closure"}

**Invariant**: Every trajectory must have explicit admission, continuation, and termination conditions.

**Implication**: An implementation that can begin work but cannot prove why it should continue or stop does not have a complete control contract.

:::

::: {#pri-state-provenance .callout-principle title="State needs provenance"}

**Invariant**: Persistent state is useful only when its origin, version, and authority can be established at the point of use.

**Implication**: Context construction and memory retrieval must preserve enough provenance to distinguish current evidence from stale, derived, or untrusted material.

:::

::: {#pri-authority-budget .callout-principle title="Authority is a consumable budget"}

**Invariant**: A trajectory can exercise only the capabilities granted within its current scope, time, and resource budget.

**Implication**: Capability checks belong in the execution path, and broader authority requires correspondingly stronger verification and recovery.

:::
